newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SAYS SUMMIT WON'T DELAY ACCESSION.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SAYS SUMMIT WON'T DELAY ACCESSION.

text.p: Hungary said on Wednesday the outcome of the European Union's Amsterdam summit would not delay the country's EU accession process.
"The most important thing is that the results and shortcomings of the summit will not slow down the start of the (EU's) enlargement," Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs told Reuters.
Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic are widely regarded as the frontrunners for EU membership.
"Accession talks would start as originally planned, six months after the inter-governmental conference," Kovacs said.
He added that he was not particularly concerned about the delay of the EU's institutional reform and further delays could even prove beneficial to Hungary.
"If this does not hinder the enlargement it would not bother us if they would wait for us to join before deciding on some matters, because then we would also have a say," Kovacs said.

Kovacs told a news conference that while Hungary would like to see accession talks first started with the most prepared countries, he understood the EU's reasons for initiating talks with all 11 applicants at the same time.
However, he added that Hungary did not wish to be delayed in joining the Union by other, less prepared candidates.
"We do not want to see a convoy-effect where the speed is determined by the slowest mover," Kovacs said.
He said Hungary hopes that it would conclude accession talks with the EU by the year 2000 and member countries would ratify Hungary's membership by 2002.
Kovacs said that during his meetings with EU officials Hungary's timetable for accession was qualified as "ambitious but not unrealistic".
